:::{#thm-data-processing-inequality}
#### Data processing inequality

If $X \to Y \to Z$ is a [Markov chain](#def-markov-chain)
and the [entropies](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-entropy) of $X$, $Y$ and $Z$ are finite,
then

$$\mutinfof{X}{Z} \le \mutinfof{X}{Y}.$$

:::

::: {.proof}

The [chain rule](#thm-mutual-information-chain-rule) for the pair $(Z, Y)$ and the pair $(Y, Z)$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mutinfof{Z, Y}{X} &= \mutinfof{Y}{X} + \cmutinfof{Z}{X}{Y} \\
\mutinfof{Y, Z}{X} &= \mutinfof{Z}{X} + \cmutinfof{Y}{X}{Z}.
\end{aligned}
$$

The pairs $(Z, Y)$ and $(Y, Z)$ contain the same two variables,
so $\mutinfof{Z, Y}{X} = \mutinfof{Y, Z}{X}$.
By @lem-markov-chain-conditional-mutual-information, $\cmutinfof{Z}{X}{Y} = 0$.
By @thm-conditional-mutual-information-nonnegative, $\cmutinfof{Y}{X}{Z} \ge 0$.
Therefore

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mutinfof{Y}{X}
&= \mutinfof{Z}{X} + \cmutinfof{Y}{X}{Z} \\
&\ge \mutinfof{Z}{X}.
\end{aligned}
$$

By @thm-mutual-information-symmetric,
$\mutinfof{Y}{X} = \mutinfof{X}{Y}$ and $\mutinfof{Z}{X} = \mutinfof{X}{Z}$,
so $\mutinfof{X}{Z} \le \mutinfof{X}{Y}$.

:::
